column1: # Per-cycle-normalized tau on raw records, 10/18. Li-ion only, readout + R_FIRST, geo_bins, 3 seeds. Same as
#   sweep_10_17_raw.tsv except tau: RAW_TAU=cycle_norm -> tau = 300 * step / that cycle's duration (rests included), so
#   every cycle sums to tau 300 like the 300-point grid (300 steps x tau 1), but every logged record stays in and the
#   real spacing inside a cycle is kept. The first record of each cycle (gap since the previous cycle) gets RAW_TAU_BND:
#   1 vs 0 is the ablation (0 = that record does not write to the state).
# Question: does per-cycle time normalization (what the grid did implicitly) recover S4D's grid result on raw records?
#   Compare to: S4D grid off 0.203 / tdtconst 0.208 / tdtreal 0.261; S4D raw const 0.260 / real 0.252 (2 seeds);
#   Mamba grid tdtconst 0.260 / tdtreal 0.260; Mamba raw const / real (pending).
# DT_C=5 x DT_CLIP=100 = steps capped at 500 s before normalizing (only non-logging pauses), same cap as the raw real arm.
# Not built: separate charge / discharge normalization (150 + 150 like the grid, rests own share) -- option (b);
#   log(cycle duration) on the R token. Run test_raw.py first (numpy cycle_norm checks; --data --raw_tau_mode cycle_norm).
